headline: MIDAS MINERALS HITS 22.6M AT 6.01% COPPER EQUIVALENT — T-13 DEPOSIT EYES LARGER RESOURCE AS ASSAYS STILL PENDING
snippet: Midas Minerals (ASX: MM1) delivered standout T-13 copper-silver results at the Otavi Copper Project in Namibia on October 6, with the latest intercept returning 22.6 metres at 6.01% copper equivalent from 347.5 metres — part of a campaign that has also intersected 50 metres averaging 5.55% copper and 125 g/t silver in earlier infill holes. Eleven additional drill holes at T-13 remain pending assay with two diamond rigs still active, and an updated mineral resource estimate is expected later in 2026.

headline: GOLDEN BOULDER CONFIRMS 4M AT 11.38 G/T GOLD — 1.1KM OF 3.5KM STRIKE NOW DRILLED IN DUKETON, WA
source_name: Discovery Alert / Great Southern Mining (ASX: GSN)
snippet: Great Southern Mining (ASX: GSN) extended the Golden Boulder discovery to 1.1 km of confirmed gold mineralisation within a 3.5 km prospective strike at its Duketon Gold Project in Western Australia, with October 6 results headlined by 4 metres at 11.38 g/t gold alongside multiple additional high-grade intervals. Golden Boulder sits between Regis Resources' multi-million-ounce Duketon deposits and Genesis Minerals' Laverton tenure, and the company says the system now warrants a systematic drill-out of the full 3.7-kilometre trend.

headline: CENTINELA STRIKE ELIGIBLE OCT. 13, ESCONDIDA SUPERVISORS REJECT BHP — CHILE COPPER LABOR WALL BUILDS
snippet: Workers at Antofagasta's Centinela mine are legally eligible to begin a work stoppage on October 13 after rejecting the company's final collective agreement offer and completing mandatory mediation, while Escondida supervisors separately voted 95% in favour of strike action and entered their own five-day government-led mediation with BHP. The simultaneous standoffs at two of Chile's largest copper operations are providing a supply-risk floor for LME copper prices above $14,000 per tonne even as a stronger dollar creates headwinds.

headline: GOLD BULLS SIDELINED AS USD HITS 2026 HIGH — GDXJ DOWN 9%, FOMC OCT 27-28 NOW THE BINARY CATALYST
snippet: Gold is trading between $4,138 and $4,179 per ounce as the U.S. dollar index reaches a fresh year-to-date high and the 10-year Treasury yield holds near 5.22%, keeping speculative buyers sidelined despite near-zero October Fed rate hike odds following the September payrolls miss. The GDXJ junior miner ETF has fallen more than 9% over the past month — declining 2–5 times harder than spot gold — as record central bank buying of 289 tonnes fails to lift equities, leaving the October 27–28 FOMC as the binary event that determines whether miners break higher or retest the September lows.

headline: SUNSHINE METALS 4M AT 11.11 G/T GOLD FROM 62M AT SYBIL — NEAR-PLANT DISCOVERY COULD FAST-TRACK TO PRODUCTION
snippet: Sunshine Metals (ASX: SHN) reported 4 metres at 11.11 g/t gold from 62 metres depth at the Sybil low-sulphidation epithermal project in Queensland, where proximity to the company's existing Mt Moss processing plant creates a potential fast-track development path if the high-grade zone proves continuous. The result is part of an RC and diamond drilling campaign launched in July 2026 after airborne surveying identified multiple vein targets across the Sybil corridor, with additional holes and assays pending.

headline: MANHATTAN GOLD MAIDEN SPECTRE DRILL: 6.1M AT 3.18% CU, 147.9 G/T AG — FIRST MODERN HOLES SINCE 1974
snippet: Manhattan Gold Corporation (ASX: MHC) announced maiden October 6 results from the Spectre VMS polymetallic target in Nunavut, with the first modern drill hole since 1974 returning 6.10 metres at 3.18% copper, 147.9 g/t silver, 1.37 g/t gold, and 1.35% zinc from 45.72 metres — testing continuity of massive sulphide lenses that previous operators had only explored to approximately 61 metres vertical depth. Additional holes from the inaugural Spectre program are pending assay alongside results from the Jaws, Quantum, and Lotus gold targets.

headline: LODE RESOURCES MONTEZUMA: MOORES LODE DELIVERS 1,241 G/T SILVER EQUIVALENT — FIVE HIGH-GRADE HITS IN TASMANIA
snippet: Lode Resources (ASX: LDR) reported five high-grade intercepts from the Montezuma project in Tasmania on October 6, headlined by the newly discovered Moores Lode returning 1,241 g/t silver equivalent over 1.0 metre in drill hole MZS43 — extending a VMS-style replacement system in the same Palaeozoic belt as the historic Rosebery and Hercules mines. Each round of drilling at Montezuma has identified new high-grade zones, and the expanding target inventory is expected to support an updated resource estimate covering the silver-antimony-zinc system.

headline: ROKMASTER SPUDS FIRST HOLE AT BC'S MYSTERY PORPHYRY — 500M IP TARGET UNTOUCHED SINCE KENNCO AND NORANDA
snippet: Rokmaster Resources Corp. (TSXV: RKR) collared the first-ever diamond drill hole on the Mystery Property in British Columbia in early October 2026, testing a central high-resistivity anomaly to approximately 500 metres depth that was outlined by an IP survey conducted by SJ Geophysics in June. Previous operators including Kennco, Noranda, and Copper Mountain Mining advanced the porphyry copper-molybdenum-gold targets since 1969 without ever drilling them; results are expected late Q4 2026 and could add a second pipeline project alongside Rokmaster's active Hanson copper-gold program.

headline: CAULDRON ENERGY YANREY: 100 HOLES LINK MANYINGEE NORTH TO PALADIN'S DEPOSIT — JORC UPDATE DUE WITHIN 2 MONTHS
snippet: Cauldron Energy (ASX: CXU) completed the 2026 Yanrey uranium drill campaign — 100 holes and 10,506 metres — confirming that the Manyingee North zone extends continuously into the ground immediately adjacent to Paladin Energy's Manyingee deposit, quadrupling the strike length covered by the current resource polygon. An updated JORC resource estimate is expected within two months, a potential re-rating catalyst as Western Australia's uranium permitting environment continues to evolve and in-situ recovery projects near operational baselines attract renewed attention.

headline: ATOMIC EAGLE HITS 86% URANIUM RECOVERY WITH JUST 3 KG/T ACID — ZAMBIA HEAP-LEACH CASE STRENGTHENED
snippet: Atomic Eagle (ASX: AEU) reported October 2026 metallurgical testwork from the Muntanga East uranium project in Zambia delivering 81–86% uranium recovery from low-grade core using approximately 3 kilograms per tonne of acid — low reagent consumption that makes a heap-leach development model economically compelling for the large-footprint, shallow deposit. The results de-risk a key technical variable ahead of a scoping study, positioning Muntanga East as one of the few near-development uranium assets outside the traditional Athabasca Basin and Australian Tier-1 jurisdictions.
